wa_south_face_4.approach: The Temple (Kangaroo Temple, on Kangaroo Ridge) is reached from the large pullout at the hairpin turns on SR-20 just east of Washington Pass — the same parking area used for the neighboring Hairpin Crags/Spire Gully climbs. From the pullout, a climber's trail heads south across a boulder field, through forest and more talus (faint, intermittently cairned) up to Kangaroo Pass, about 1 hour. From the pass, an intermittent trail traverses to a gully between Kangaroo Temple and Little Finger; ascending or descending that gully reaches the base of the North Face, Northwest Face, or Southwest Face routes, roughly another hour. Total trailhead-to-summit time runs about 7-8 hours round trip. IMPORTANT — this route uses a genuinely different approach than Temple's North/Northwest Face routes: park at the same hairpin pullout but hike southeast on the right side of the creek on a trail that improves past several slide/boulder areas, never crossing Kangaroo Pass. Longer and steeper, and the face isn't visible from the highway.

wa_the_l_h_route_free_variation.fa: Original aid line: Jim Langdon and Mead Hargis, 1969

wa_prusik_peak_prayer_for_a_friend.overview: The hardest documented route on Prusik Peak: a 5.14a big-wall-style testpiece up the south face headwall, first aided by Fitz Cahall and freed by Adrian Vanoni.
